correspondence.component_scope: Saint John–Rolla headward drainage and western Big Coulee
correspondence.finding: Overlapping original maps show the selected intermittent headward corridor near Saint John and Rolla, with small ponds and wet depressions rather than a named major source lake. The route continues southeast and east in the western drainage past the Perth/Bisbee area; the state map places a Big Coulee stream label on this branch before its meeting with Mauvais Coulee. Nearby McGillis Creek, Hidden Island Coulee and the main Mauvais headward branch near Rock Lake are distinguishable other corridors and are not substituted for the selected western route.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward corridor and its connection to the western Big Coulee branch covered at ordinary map scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Uppermost feeder name remains null. Big Coulee is supported on the mapped western branch; the surrounding Mauvais Coulee administrative-basin label is not used as a name for every headward channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Big Coulee–Mauvais Coulee junction and shared route to Lake Alice
correspondence.finding: The western branch joins the separately mapped Mauvais Coulee northeast of Cando. Original cartography follows the shared southerly channel east of Cando and toward Lake Alice, through wetland and widened-channel reaches. USGS prose independently identifies Mauvais Coulee as an inflow to Lake Alice.
correspondence.correspondence: Material junction and downstream lake entry inspected.
correspondence.name_scope: Mauvais Coulee is supported for this named trunk component; its name is not extended through all later lakes.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Alice–Lake Irvine passage
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation turns southwest through the Lake Alice and Lake Irvine setting. Both original maps depict their relationship and connecting low-water/wetland passage. Chain Lake and Mikes Lake lie to the east as distinct connected lake components. USGS prose explicitly describes a channel connecting Alice to Irvine and the Irvine outlet to Big Coulee.
correspondence.correspondence: Lake-to-lake connection covered; different mapped water extents are treated as hydrologic-stage differences, not missing correspondence.
correspondence.name_scope: Lake labels are confined to their waterbody components. Chain, Mikes and Dry lakes are not falsely counted as selected through-passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Irvine outlet, downstream Big Coulee and Pelican Lake
correspondence.finding: The source maps continue the Irvine outlet through Churchs Ferry and along the narrow wetland/channel corridor beside Silver Lake into the Pelican Lake setting, then into the western Devils Lake waterbody. The state map labels Big Coulee at the outlet corridor, and USGS prose distinguishes this natural route from Channel A, which diverts Dry Lake water into Sixmile Bay. The selected route follows the western natural corridor, not Channel A.
correspondence.correspondence: Irvine outlet, corridor beside Silver Lake, Pelican passage and Devils Lake entry covered.
correspondence.name_scope: Big Coulee is the source-supported name for the outlet corridor. It is not assigned to Pelican Lake, Devils Lake, or the entire selected system.

correspondence.component_scope: Devils Lake and eastern continuation
correspondence.finding: Original cartography shows the selected eastward passage across Devils Lake, south of the city and through the eastern lake continuation into East Devils Lake. Broad inundated areas, arms, peninsulas, road crossings and the distinction between the main lake and the eastern named lake provide ordinary corridor correspondence. The selected line is a modeled lake traversal, not an independently observed river centerline across the lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Western-to-eastern lake passage and East Devils Lake entry covered.
correspondence.name_scope: Devils Lake and East Devils Lake are waterbody names, not inferred river names.

correspondence.component_scope: East Devils Lake–Swan Lake–Stump Lake terminal
correspondence.finding: The original maps show the eastern low corridor from East Devils Lake toward Swan Lake, its connection into Stump Lake, and the selected terminal within the Stump Lake setting. The 2006 map distinguishes channel/wetland connections under its circa-2003 water extents; USGSTopo shows much broader joined water. The route does not continue to the Sheyenne River. Official state prose identifies Devils Lake and Stump Lake as closed-basin lakes with large climate-driven changes and historical overflow episodes.
correspondence.correspondence: Final material connector, lake entry and actual selected terminal covered.
correspondence.name_scope: Swan Lake and Stump Lake remain lake labels. Stump Lake basin is not used as a representative river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Serra do Caparaó headward approach and Alto Caparaó
correspondence.finding: The Alto Caparaó original maps the selected upland approach west of the principal Caparaó divide, connected to the Rio Caparaó east/northeast of Alto Caparaó. It follows that river southwest toward the town and then south, while separately depicting Córrego Três Barras and the Rio José Pedro drainage beyond the divide. The initial tip is not assigned a separate spring name.

correspondence.component_scope: Alto Caparaó–Caparaó–Pedra Menina continuation
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Alto Caparaó, Caparaó and Espera Feliz originals follow the southward Rio Caparaó past Pinheiros, the São Pedro/Boa Esperança setting and Caparaó, continuing through Empossado and São José da Pedra Menina toward Espera Feliz. Ribeirão São Domingos and the eastern Rio Preto are separately depicted watercourses. No lake crossing is required by this headward route.

correspondence.component_scope: Espera Feliz junction and Caiana continuation
correspondence.finding: The Espera Feliz original shows the selected northern Rio Caparaó approach meeting Rio São João arriving from the São Sebastião da Barra side. The river continues south through Espera Feliz and Caiana as São João. The Caiana sheet overlaps the entire continuation and distinguishes the western São Roque/Funil tributary approaches and the eastern Bananal/Mato Grosso branches.

correspondence.component_scope: Divininho and São João–Preto formation of Itabapoana
correspondence.finding: The Caiana original maps São João southeast and south past the Serra da Queixada, Santa Cruz and Divininho setting, then southeast to the Três Estados junction. Rio Preto arrives separately from the northeast along the Minas Gerais–Espírito Santo boundary. The downstream channel is explicitly labeled Rio Itabapoana, and turns east along the Espírito Santo–Rio de Janeiro boundary. This directly accounts for the selected western headward choice and name transition.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Itabapoana boundary valley toward Rosal
correspondence.finding: The state-map original continues the same boundary river east below São Pedro de Rates and then south west of Guaçuí toward the Rosal/Airituba valley. It distinguishes the Ribeirão da Onça entering from the Santa Clara side and Rio do Veado from the Guaçuí side. The Bom Jesus original overlaps the southern continuation, including the Prata/Rosal Volta Grande approach. These are continuous mapped valley connections, not identity inferred from an encompassing basin label.

correspondence.component_scope: Rosal reservoir and downstream natural-river corridor
correspondence.finding: The Bom Jesus original explicitly maps Reservatório Rosal as an expanded, branched waterbody along the selected boundary river below the Volta Grande setting, with the Usina Hidrelétrica Rosal label at its southern end. The river continues south through the Rosal/Airituba setting. Reservoir side arms are distinguished from the through-going selected corridor. Previously read field-study prose separately identifies a reservoir sampling reach and the reduced-flow reach below Rosal.

correspondence.component_scope: Calheiros hydropower connection, Pirapetinga valley and Bom Jesus
correspondence.finding: The Bom Jesus map traces the river through Calheiros, Alegoria, Ponte do Vieira and Barra do Pirapetinga, past the Rio Calçado confluence and into the Bom Jesus do Itabapoana/Bom Jesus do Norte urban valley. The independent 2000 Calheiros RIMA maps its project reservoir in this same north–south river valley and documents the intake-to-powerhouse bypass while retaining the natural river channel and returning flow above Calheiros. This project evidence is distinguished from later operation: the prior-lawful 2017 study describes Calheiros, Pirapetinga and Franca Amaral among the operating sites then. No diversion tunnel is asserted to be the selected surface line.

correspondence.component_scope: Bom Jesus–Apiacá–Ponte do Itabapoana middle/lower river
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Bom Jesus and Mimoso originals map the eastward river below the twin towns, through the José Carlos/Turu and Apiacá settings, then the bend toward Ponte do Itabapoana and Santo Eduardo. The Rio Muqui do Sul and other northern tributary approaches are separately depicted. The selected line remains on Itabapoana rather than following those tributaries inland.

correspondence.component_scope: Pedra do Garrafão reservoir, outlet and BR-101 passage
correspondence.finding: The Mimoso original shows the river entering an expanded waterbody east of Santo Eduardo/Ponte do Itabapoana, with a southern side arm and an eastern constriction labeled Pequena Central Hidrelétrica Pedra do Garrafão. The river channel remains visible below the structure, continues east through several bends and reaches BR-101. Prior-lawful field-study prose independently distinguishes the reservoir, reduced-flow reach and downstream BR-101 crossing. These connections are visually mapped rather than supplied solely by the model.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Rio Itabapoana / Pedra do Garrafão reservoir setting

correspondence.component_scope: Coastal plain, lower tributaries and Atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The Mimoso and São Francisco originals overlap across the lower floodplain, showing the eastward Itabapoana through the Campinas/Passo Calçado setting, alongside separately drawn Rio Preto and local drainage. The São Francisco original continues the river past São Valentim/Terreira, turns south along the coastal plain, then east through the Barra do Itabapoana estuarine channel into the Atlantic. Nearby Lagoa Feia locality, Córrego São Paulo and coastal drains are not substituted for a selected lake crossing. The map also distinguishes the much farther south Paraíba do Sul outlet, which is not this terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern headward opening and west-northwest approach
correspondence.finding: The southern opening and first west-northwest connector occupy the national map's northern Inland Ice. The map includes the complete selected area south of the 81 degrees N southern boundary of Sheet 7. The ice surface, ice-thickness and sub-ice bedrock contour symbols are identified through the actual legend.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No mapped natural source, river trace or subglacial channel is inferred from an ice contour or model connectivity.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northward interior-ice connector
correspondence.finding: The route continues north through the broad continental-ice area east of the exposed-land belt of the inner Victoria Fjord region. The national map covers the southern portion and overlaps Sheet 7 after its 81 degrees N edge, leaving no missing inter-sheet interval.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Ice geography provides corridor correspondence; the sources do not establish that the modeled line represents a continuous visible or subglacial river.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward and northward bends before the terminal approach
correspondence.finding: The succeeding northwest and north connectors remain in the ice-covered approach east of the mapped exposed-terrain margin, south of Freuchen Land. Sheet 7 distinguishes that ice area from rock outcrops, superficial-cover patches and the separately mapped neighboring glaciers.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No separate selected lake passage, tributary junction or reservoir connector is established, and no neighboring glacier name is extended over the modeled connectors.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward terminal approach and ending setting
correspondence.finding: The final westward approach occupies the eastern ice/land-margin setting in the inner Victoria Fjord region, south of the mapped Jungersen Gletscher corridor and north of Harder Gletscher. The detailed original covers the whole approach and ending setting. The ending is not established on these maps as an ordinary named river mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terminal-corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The mapped land/ice margin and neighboring glacier/fjord context do not corroborate the model terminal class sea as a present river mouth. No contemporary shoreline, current glacier-front position or exact discharge destination is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern Green Swamp wetland headward feeder
correspondence.finding: The eastern original federal view covers the selected beginning in forested wetlands east of Old Grade Road, south of Deen Still Road. It shows the northward wetland/stream connection across the Deen Still Road setting and its continuation through the eastern Green Swamp. The selected initial feeder is distinct from the lake chain and drainage beside Commonwealth Avenue farther west. No exact spring or uniform name for the initial tip is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Turkey Creek and westward Withlacoochee approach
correspondence.finding: The same view shows the selected northward approach meeting the mapped Turkey Creek corridor in the Lake–Polk boundary setting and turning west toward SR 33. The connected watercourse continues west through Loggy Pond Swamp into the repeatedly labeled Withlacoochee River corridor near Withla and westward. The more northerly Turkey Creek and Little Creek branches, nearby ponds, and the southern Pony Creek approach are distinguishable from the selected feeder. This is direct geographic coverage, not an inference from the Green Swamp basin label.

correspondence.component_scope: Green Swamp westward bend and northward course east of Dade City
correspondence.finding: The overlapping eastern and western federal views trace the river southwest through the Rock Ridge and Withlacoochee River Swamp settings, west across SR 471, and around the broad bend north of US 98 before it turns north east of Dade City. The western view continues past the riverine lakes and swamps to Lacoochee. Pony Creek, Colt/Gator Creek approaches, the southwestern Hillsborough overflow, Devils Creek and Gator Hole Slough remain separate connecting branches rather than alternate names for the entire selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: Lacoochee, Ridge Manor and Silver Lake
correspondence.finding: DEP maps 1–2 continue from Lacoochee past the CR 575 bend, Ridge Manor and Croom into the Silver Lake setting and onward to Nobleton. The Little Withlacoochee enters near River Junction and southern Silver Lake; its eastern approach is not the selected headward route.

correspondence.component_scope: Nobleton to Outlet River and Wysong
correspondence.finding: DEP maps 3–4 show the selected corridor past Istachatta, Lake Annie, Nelson Lake and Bonnet Lake, then Princess Lake, the Outlet River connection from Lake Panasoffkee, Carlson/Wysong and Rutland. Panasoffkee is east of the main route; its Outlet River is the lateral connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Tsala Apopka lateral connections and middle-river junctions
correspondence.finding: The district maps distinguish the selected river east of the Floral City, Inverness and Hernando pools. Jumper Creek and Outlet River enter from the east. Orange State and Leslie Heifner canals and northern marsh/canal connections link Tsala Apopka to the river without making all its pools a selected mainstem passage. Wysong is downstream of Outlet River.

correspondence.component_scope: Rutland, Potts Preserve, Stokes Ferry and Dunnellon
correspondence.finding: DEP maps 5–7 trace the river past the Gum Slough/Gum Springs Run junction and Potts Preserve, northwest through Stokes Ferry and Two Mile Prairie, then to Dunnellon. The Rainbow River enters from the north at Dunnellon. The federal coastal view overlaps this junction and the westward continuation.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Rousseau and altered Inglis outlet
correspondence.finding: The federal map follows the selected westward route through the broad Lake Rousseau impoundment and its southwestern old-river outlet. District figures 18-1–18-2 identify Inglis Dam, the Barge Canal, Inglis Lock and the separate Bypass Channel to the lower river. The report explains that canal construction severed the former river course and a bypass conveys normal flows. This known alteration is covered, not an unread connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Withlacoochee and Bird Creek-side terminal estuary
correspondence.finding: The coastal federal view shows the lower river continuing west past the US 19 crossing and the Inglis–Yankeetown riverfront, then turning southwest into the tidal marsh. The selected final westward and northwestward bend occupies the Bird Creek-side outlet network north of the main river navigation exit. Bird Creek, Bennetts Creek and Johns Creek are separately labeled, and the straight Cross Florida Barge Canal lies farther south. The endpoint is assessed as this connected estuarine/coastal setting, not recast as the exact open-Gulf mouth of a uniformly named river.
